title: Latency Chorus: comparative SLI matrix by model, route and IO pattern
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create an integrated latency SLI matrix (p50/p95/p99) that compares model routes with explicit IO-pattern breakdowns (io_pattern tags such as streaming, blocking, continued_stream). The goal is a single dashboard that helps SREs and ML platform engineers quickly identify route-level regressions, streaming vs non-streaming tail behavior, and correlated error spikes. This ticket covers: (1) tracing hook adjustments to tag spans with route/model/io_pattern, (2) metric ingestion changes and pre-aggregation of latency histograms, (3) dashboard panels and drilldowns linking traces, logs and cohort playback. Emphasis on practical SLOs, cost-aware pre-aggregation, and trace sampling that preserves tail fidelity.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Dashboard surfaces p50/p95/p99 for each model+route combination and shows column split for io_pattern values (streaming, blocking, background).
2) Panels link to trace view within 1 click with filters pre-populated (model, route, io_pattern, timeframe).
3) Metric pipeline emits pre-aggregated quantile-aware histograms with max 2x storage overhead compared to current summaries.
4) Tracing hooks add io_pattern tag for >95% of production sampled requests after rollout.
5) Alert rules for >=30% p95 increase over baseline for any route are created with runbook link.
comments: 2026-02-25 - Ava Chen: Kickoff. Initial notes: this grew out of recurring on-call incidents where streaming tails diverged and existing dashboards only showed endpoint-level percentiles without IO splits. Drafted PRD and sketch in Confluence (link below).

2026-02-27 - Mateo Ruiz: Implementation plan: (A) Add io_pattern tagging at router layer in servepath; (B) Update OpenTelemetry tracer config to propagate io_pattern in span attributes; (C) Add histogram bucketization job in metrics pipeline (ClickHouse rollups) to enable accurate pXX queries; (D) Grafana dashboard with composite table + sparklines per route/model. Estimate 5 points.

2026-03-02 - UX Review (Lina Park): Mockups reviewed. Feedback: make streaming rows sticky and expose 'conversation shape' filter. UX will provide a compact row design for dense route matrices. Action: Lina to drop SVG mocks in Confluence by 2026-03-05.

2026-03-04 - Infra (J. Patel): We should avoid high-cardinality tags in metrics aggregation. Recommendation: map io_pattern to a small enum (streaming|sync|background) upstream, preserve original verb in logs only. Suggested pre-aggregation key: (model, route, io_pattern, minute).

2026-03-07 - Mateo Ruiz: Proof-of-concept implemented on staging. Changes: added io_pattern span attribute in tracer; updated collector pipeline to enrich metrics with io_pattern via <router id>. Verified with synthetic load. p95 for streaming route 'chat-complete' shows expected tail. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/servepath/pull/984 (wip).

2026-03-10 - On-call postmortem link added: During incident INC-2026-0310 we noticed p99 divergence for streaming-only workloads. This dashboard will be part of the runbook to identify if degradation is model-level, route-level, or IO-pattern specific.
2026-03-11 - Security review (note): No customer data fields are added; io_pattern is non-sensitive. Security: approved as low risk.
next_steps: 1) Merge tracing hook PR and rollout to canary (owner: Mateo). 2) Deploy metrics pre-aggregation in ClickHouse staging and validate quantiles via synthetic queries (owner: Infra). 3) Finalize Grafana panels with UX compact rows and add trace link actions (owner: Lina + Mateo). 4) Post rollout, run a 72h fidelity check to ensure p99 matches sampled traces within expected error bounds. 5) Create alerts and document in runbook.
notes: Trade-offs considered: full high-cardinality io_pattern strings would give richer analytics but explode metric dimensions and storage; we standardize to a 3-value enum for metrics and retain raw IO labels in logs/traces for one-off investigations. We chose pre-aggregated histogram rollups to keep dashboard queries fast; this requires a small additional storage budget but reduces on-query CPU. Trace sampling rate bumped to 2% for all streamed routes during canary to ensure tail capture; will tune down after assessment.
